svg.title: The distinctions are reachable with deliberation
svg.desc: Left, bars for the 15 judgments whose reasoning finished: direct scoring by the original model without reasoning, 9 of 15 correct; our trained single-pass judge, 13 of 15; reasoning by the original model, 15 of 15. Right, two tiles: our trained judge takes 0.18 seconds per five-question request; reasoning takes 41 seconds per question, about 3,000 thinking tokens, and 15 of 30 questions hit the 4,096-token cap. Notes state that the 30 held-out judgments cover one case per semantic category and one question per primitive, that the finished traces are selected by termination, that over all 30 reasoning answered 15 correctly, our judge 23 and direct scoring 13, and that reasoning used 90,289 thinking tokens in 20.3 minutes.

g.font-family: Cambria, Georgia, Times New Roman, serif
g.text: The distinctions are reachable with deliberation
Original Qwen3.5-2B allowed up to 4,096 thinking tokens, compared with single-pass judgment.
Correct on the 15 judgments whose reasoning finished
30 held-out judgments: one case per semantic category, one question per primitive. The 15 finished traces are selected
by termination; over all 30, reasoning answered 15 correctly, our judge 23 and direct scoring 13.
Reasoning used 90,289 thinking tokens in 20.3 minutes. Timings on one shared RTX 4080.
